questions.questionText: The radius of a nucleus is proportional to:
questions.solution: R = R0*A^(1/3) where A is mass number.
Nuclear density is about 2.3 x 10^17 kg/m^3, independent of mass number.

questions.optionB: Difference between sum of nucleon masses and actual nuclear mass
questions.solution: Mass defect = Z*mp + (A-Z)*mn - M_nucleus.

questions.questionText: Binding energy per nucleon is maximum for:
questions.solution: BE/A peaks around A=56 (iron) at about 8.75 MeV/nucleon.

questions.optionB: Splitting a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei
questions.solution: Fission splits a heavy nucleus into two or more lighter fragments.

questions.optionB: Combining light nuclei to form heavier nucleus
questions.solution: Fusion combines light nuclei releasing energy.

questions.questionText: The half-life of a radioactive element is:
questions.optionA: Time for all atoms to decay
questions.optionB: Time for half the atoms to decay
questions.optionD: Time for activity to become zero
questions.solution: Half-life is the time for half the radioactive nuclei to decay.

questions.questionText: In alpha decay the mass number changes by:
questions.solution: Alpha particle has A=4 so parent mass number decreases by 4.

questions.optionD: A gamma ray is emitted only
questions.solution: In beta-minus decay: n -> p + e- + antineutrino.
N = N0 * e^(-lambda*t), exponential decay.

questions.questionText: The relation between half-life and decay constant is:
questions.solution: T_(1/2) = ln2/lambda = 0.693/lambda.
Nuclear (strong) forces are short range (~1-3 fm) and much stronger than electromagnetic forces.

questions.optionC: Neither mass number nor atomic number changes
questions.solution: Gamma decay releases energy as photon; A and Z remain unchanged.

questions.questionText: The activity of a radioactive sample is:
questions.solution: Activity A = |dN/dt| = lambda*N.

questions.questionText: The SI unit of radioactivity is:
questions.solution: SI unit is Becquerel (1 Bq = 1 disintegration per second).
Stars fuse hydrogen into helium releasing enormous energy.

questions.optionA: Same mass number different atomic number
questions.optionB: Same atomic number different mass number
questions.solution: Isotopes: same Z (protons) different A (mass number).

questions.optionC: Attractive at moderate distance repulsive at very short distance
questions.solution: Nuclear force is attractive at ~1 fm but becomes repulsive at < 0.7 fm.

questions.questionText: After 3 half-lives the fraction of undecayed nuclei is:
questions.solution: After n half-lives: N/N0 = (1/2)^n = (1/2)^3 = 1/8.
James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.questionText: The mass of a proton is approximately:
questions.solution: Proton mass is approximately 1.67 x 10^-27 kg.

questions.questionText: Nuclear fission was first demonstrated with:
questions.solution: Hahn and Strassmann first demonstrated fission of U-235.

questions.questionText: Mean life of a radioactive element is:
questions.solution: Mean life tau = 1/lambda = T_(1/2)/ln2. Both expressions are equivalent.

questions.optionA: Needed to hold electrons in orbit
questions.optionB: Required to break nucleus into individual nucleons
questions.solution: Binding energy is the energy needed to disassemble a nucleus into free nucleons.
